findings.title: Test cleanup registers removal of literal IDP alias "alias" instead of the created aliases
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` (also repeated at line 425 for "idp-alias-20"). The literal string "alias" is used instead of the loop variable `alias` ("idp-alias-" + i), so the cleanup targets a non-existent identity provider. As a result, the 21 IDPs created by the test (10 of which are explicitly linked to organization "orga" via addIdentityProvider) are never removed from the test realm. Besides leaking brokers between tests in the same realm, this can break other tests in the class that assert on IDP counts per organization — e.g. testCacheIDPByOrg asserts `assertEquals(6, identityProviderListQuery.getIDPs("-1.-1").size())` for orga, which would fail if the leftover orga-linked IDPs from testCacheIDPForLogin are still present, depending on test execution order.

findings.title: No test removes a login-eligible IDP to verify login cache invalidation on removal
findings.body: The new `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` code path in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove() is only exercised in the test with "idp-alias-1", which is disabled and therefore never present in the login caches. There is no test that removes an IDP that actually appears in the cached getForLogin results (e.g. one of the enabled "idp-alias-0/2/4..." providers) and asserts that the FetchMode caches are invalidated and repopulated without the removed IDP. Since removal invalidation depends on evaluating the login predicate against the model fetched from the delegate before deletion, a regression in this new logic (e.g. evaluating the predicate on the wrong model or skipping invalidation) would go undetected.

findings.title: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate evaluates the login predicate on the organization-aware wrapper, causing spurious invalidations
findings.body: In update(), the `original` model passed to registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate comes from getById(), which returns a model wrapped by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. That wrapper overrides isEnabled() to return false whenever the linked organization is missing or disabled. The login predicate (which uses IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled) therefore reports the original IDP as not login-eligible even though the stored IDP itself is enabled, public and not hidden. For any update of an org-linked IDP whose organization is disabled (or has been removed), the skip conditions in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate are bypassed and all three login cache entries (REALM_ONLY, ORG_ONLY, ALL) are invalidated cluster-wide on every trivial update (e.g. a displayName change), defeating the cache. Correctness is not affected, but the invalidation can be avoided by fetching the raw stored model from idpDelegate (as done in remove()) instead of using the wrapped getById() result.
